lens: Vercel Geist design language: monochrome precision, Geist Sans/Mono, hairline borders, shadcn/ui
name: Geist Signal Console
one_liner: A monochrome dev-tool console for sales reps: Geist type and hairlines for calm, with one teal signal that lights only when the AI coach has something to say.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Geist lens: Geist Sans and Geist Mono loaded through the geist package (vercel.com/font), weights 400/500/600 only, 1px hairline borders (#EBEBEB), black primary buttons, and shadcn/ui on Radix. Changed two things. Pure monochrome reads cold to a sales audience and invites a Vercel clone (designsystems.one warns about both), so one teal signal (#14B8A6, the existing brand accent) is reserved for live AI state, and the blurry orb becomes a 1px signal ring that pulses only while the coach has a cue. Dark mode is designed first, as Geist does. Council self-scores: A 8, B 7.5, C 6.5, D 6.5, E 6.5, F1 6, F2 6.5, F3 3.

palette.use: Primary text and black primary buttons
Secondary text and speaker names (AA on white)
Meta text and mono timestamps (AA on white)
Live coach state only: ring, rule and dot. Never body text
Objection alerts, amber provenance and inferred-field text
End and grade outline and error text (AA)
Dark page background, live console default

design_language.typography: Geist Sans at 400, 500 and 600 only, never 700. Display 48px/52px at -0.03em; section heads 28px/32px; body 15px/24px; dense tables 14px/20px. Geist Mono at 400 and 500 for timers, scores, timestamps, weights, model chips and 12px uppercase eyebrows. Tabular numerals on every score and meter.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Hairline 1px borders instead of shadows. Radius 6px for controls, 8px for cards, 12px for sheets. Shadows only on floating layers (Sheet, command palette, coach toast) at 0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.12). No gradients and no blurred orb; the signal ring is the only glow.
design_language.motion: 150ms ease for hover and focus (Geist default). 240ms ease-out for the coach card entrance with an 8px rise. Rubric meters tween over 400ms. The signal ring breathes on a 2.4s cycle only while a cue is live. Everything drops to instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 16px with 1.5px stroke. One icon per action; every coach state pairs its icon with a text label so color is never the only cue. No emoji anywhere in the product.
design_language.theme_modes: Light and dark designed together. Dark is canonical for the live console. Dark tokens: canvas #000000, surface #0A0A0A, hairline #1F1F1F, ink #EDEDED, ink-2 #A1A1A1, signal #2DD4BF. Follows the OS setting, with a manual toggle in the top bar.

navigation_and_ia: Left shadcn Sidebar, collapsing to an icon rail: Practice, Library, Progress, Team (role-gated), Settings. Top bar: breadcrumb plus a cmdk command palette on Cmd-K or slash (search personas, start a call, jump to a debrief). Routes: / landing, /library (replaces /trainer/scenarios), /library/new (wizard), /practice/[scenario] (pre-call), /practice/[id]/live (live call), /debrief/[id], /progress, /team, /settings. Old URLs redirect. Mobile: bottom tab bar with Practice, Library, Progress, Team and More. The talk track and coach open as Vaul drawers. Login, MFA and access-code pages are rebuilt from the same shadcn Card and Form primitives, and the demo-mode banner becomes a hairline strip under the top bar.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The persona stays forbidden to coach. A separate coach lane runs beside it: each caller turn triggers one structured call to gpt-4.1-mini with the last turns, the rubric and the talk-track state. It returns one cue, rubric deltas, objection flags and an evidence line. Budgets: first cue within 2 seconds (p50) after the caller stops; rubric meters within 4 seconds after the rep stops; at most one cue per turn. Every cue shows its evidence and offers Accept, Dismiss and Not helpful, and that feedback becomes a contributor eval set. Live scores are labeled provisional and replaced by the graded result in the debrief. In voice mode, cues can be whispered through low-volume TTS (opt-in), with text always visible in the rail.
persona_library_and_wizard: A persona is a versioned JSON file validated by one zod schema: role, industry, seniority, temperament sliders from 0 to 10, objections, opener, rubric, voice, difficulty from 1 to 3, and license. Launch target: 200 persona-and-scenario pairs across 20 industry packs (home services, solar, insurance, mortgage, real estate, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections, SDR cold calls, AE discovery, SaaS, and more). Each pack is a folder that contributors can PR. Filters: role, industry, difficulty, objection type. The wizard sends transcripts, job descriptions, URLs, CRM notes or an ICP through one structured-output call. Every generated field either quotes its source or is marked inferred. Flow: dry-run, then save or Export as PR.
signature_moments: The signal ring: a 1px teal ring pulses only while the coach has a cue. The caller never gets color.
Meters that tick: each rep turn moves rubric meters by a mono delta such as +4, so the score feels live without flashing.
Show in transcript: any evidence quote scrolls the transcript to the exact turn and highlights it, in the live call and the debrief.
Found, then generated: the wizard lists what it found in your source, with quote chips, before it drafts a single field.
Export as PR: one click turns a persona into a JSON file and a pull-request draft.
Provenance chips: every AI output shows its model and latency, so a reviewer can see exactly which OpenAI model did the work.
openai_fund_angle: The UI makes OpenAI usage visible and legible. Every AI output carries a provenance chip with model and latency, and the dashboard shows cost per session so reviewers can see API spend. Model roles are named in the product: gpt-4.1-mini for grading and live cues, gpt-4.1 with Structured Outputs for the persona wizard, and a planned OpenAI Realtime voice adapter that we do not claim until it ships (voice is ElevenLabs today). The contributor path is the showcase: a persona is a JSON file, the wizard exports it as a PR, and CI validates it against the schema. The maintainer side fits Codex for Open Source: planned Codex PR review and release automation, with a Built with Codex credit in CONTRIBUTING.md. No OpenAI logo without permission; text credit only.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (S): add geist, run shadcn init on Tailwind 3, move colors to CSS variables with light and dark sets, swap fonts, keep current routes. Phase 1 (M to L): app shell, pre-call briefing, and the live coach rail behind a feature flag, with the cue budget tested on the three existing scenarios. Phase 2 (L): library with 200 JSON personas, filters and Sheet, then the wizard. Phase 3 (M): debrief, progress, manager view and mobile sheet. Redirect old routes and retire three.js from the core. Each phase ships behind routes so the live demo keeps working.

risks: Monochrome can read cold or as a Vercel clone. Guardrails: the teal signal, warm transcript copy, and never using color as the only cue.
Geist license: confirm the font license in vercel/geist-font before shipping as open source. The shadcn.io reference says it may be proprietary, so this is unverified.
The 2 second p50 cue budget depends on provider speed and roughly doubles per-turn API cost. Default to Silent, and add a per-session cost cap.
Current voice is ElevenLabs Agents. OpenAI Realtime voice would be a new adapter, so do not market it until built.
Library quality is the bottleneck: 200 pairs need human review, and contributor PRs will vary. Gate them with schema validation and a review checklist.
Migration from hand-rolled Tailwind to shadcn touches every screen plus auth and MFA. Keep Tailwind 3 for phase 1 and use the existing screenshot set as the regression baseline.

Viability: the SaaS market is crowded and price-pressured. One r/sales commenter (anecdotal) reports PersoneoAI at about a tenth of rivals' price. The in-call coach is the wedge. Enterprise buyers need SSO, SCIM and SOC 2, which belong in a paid tier, not the open-source core.
